$comment: Hand-written clinical scenarios used as the evaluation set. Every case states what the DETERMINISTIC gate must produce (expectedRedFlags, expectedMinimumTier) and what the full engine is expected to produce once chunk 2 lands (expectedTier). The gate assertions are the ones that must never regress: they are the safety floor. The engine assertions are allowed to be tuned. Cases are synthetic and were written to exercise the gate, not drawn from any real person.

$meta.note: A clinician must sign off this file before any real-world use. Until then it documents intended behaviour, not validated behaviour.

cases.label: Acute scrotal pain, 3 hours — possible torsion
cases.rationale: The single most time-critical presentation in male genital medicine. If this case ever routes anywhere but emergency care, the system is unsafe.

cases.label: Painless testicular lump
cases.rationale: Testicular cancer peaks in exactly this age group and is highly curable when caught early. Routing it as a fertility question would be a serious miss.

cases.label: Prolonged painful erection
cases.rationale: Priapism beyond four hours risks permanent damage. Included because it is the kind of symptom men delay reporting out of embarrassment, which is the whole problem this product addresses.

cases.label: Unable to pass urine
cases.rationale: Acute retention. Emergency regardless of any reproductive context.

cases.label: Fever with urethral discharge
cases.rationale: Febrile genitourinary infection needs same-day care and is a treatable, reversible cause of impaired fertility if caught early. This is the upstream catch the brief asks for.

cases.label: Visual field loss with gynaecomastia
cases.rationale: A prolactinoma can present as reduced libido and infertility long before anyone thinks of the pituitary. Catching it here is the clearest example of value from asking the right questions early.

cases.label: Bilateral uncorrected undescended testes
cases.rationale: Not urgent, but it changes the pathway completely and must not sit in a routine queue.

cases.label: Absent vas deferens noted previously
cases.rationale: Strongly associated with CFTR mutations, so this is a genetic counselling pathway rather than a lifestyle conversation.

cases.label: 18 months trying, obese, type 2 diabetes, current smoker
cases.rationale: The core target case. Every driver here is modifiable, and all of them are usually found late. No red flag, so this must route on risk rather than on alarm.

cases.label: 14 months trying, otherwise healthy
cases.rationale: Twelve months of trying is the conventional threshold for assessment. This case checks the pathway opens on duration alone, without needing anything to be wrong.

cases.label: 4 months trying, healthy, no symptoms
cases.rationale: Must NOT be medicalised. Over-referral here would waste capacity and teach men the service panics. Self-care information is the right answer.

cases.label: Metabolic risk, not currently trying to conceive
cases.rationale: The preventive case the brief is really about: reproductive risk found before anyone is trying, with no assumption that they intend to. Routes to primary care for the metabolic issue, and says nothing about family plans.

cases.label: Prior vasectomy, now wants to conceive
cases.rationale: Nothing is wrong and nothing needs screening. The correct answer is service navigation, not a risk score. Included because a risk-first system tends to mishandle it.

cases.label: Mumps orchitis in adolescence, 20 months trying
cases.rationale: A historical infectious cause that routine intake almost never asks about, which is precisely why it belongs in the question bank.

cases.label: Young, healthy, curious — no risk factors at all
cases.rationale: The negative control. A screening tool that cannot say “nothing to do here” is a tool that generates anxiety for a living.

cases.label: Scrotal ache with no fever, gradual onset
cases.rationale: The near-miss for GC01. Deliberately similar wording, deliberately not an emergency. If this escalates as torsion, the gate is over-triggering and will burn clinician trust.

labCases.label: Azoospermia
labCases.rationale: Must never be delivered by notification. Checks that workflow 05 withholds detail and routes to a clinician.

labCases.label: Severe oligozoospermia
labCases.rationale: Same handling as azoospermia: a clinician delivers it.

labCases.label: Mildly below reference on two parameters
labCases.rationale: WHO guidance is to repeat before concluding. Checks the pathway asks for a confirmatory sample instead of labelling.

labCases.label: Entirely within WHO 2021 reference limits
labCases.rationale: Checks that a normal result produces no flags, no escalation and no new specialist routing.
